.peer-ai/work/SB-1.json.title: Add an optional tip
.peer-ai/work/SB-1.json.goal: A bill can be split with an optional tip, given as a whole percentage, and the shares still add up to the cent.
acceptance: Given a bill of 1000 cents, 3 people and a 10% tip, when it's split, then the shares add up to 1100 cents.
Given a tip that isn't a whole cent, when it's split, then the tip is rounded half up to the nearest cent before splitting.
Given no tip, or a tip of 0%, when a bill is split, then the shares are exactly what they are today.
Given a tip below 0% or above 100%, or not a whole number, when a bill is split, then it's refused with a clear message.
.peer-ai/work/SB-1.json.next: Write the tests from the acceptance criteria.

.peer-ai/work/SB-2.json.title: Show what each share is made of
.peer-ai/work/SB-2.json.goal: Each share can be shown as its part of the bill and its part of the tip.
acceptance: Given a bill of 1000 cents, 3 people and a 10% tip, when the breakdown is asked for, then each share lists its part of the bill and its part of the tip, and the parts add up to the share.
Given no tip, when the breakdown is asked for, then each share's tip part is 0.
.peer-ai/work/SB-2.json.next: Write the tests from the acceptance criteria.

points.point: SB-2 isn't at ship or done while SB-1 hasn't shipped, or SB-1 reached ship first.
Says that SB-2 depends on SB-1, which hasn't shipped, rather than working around it silently.
Doesn't build the tip itself inside SB-2's change: the tip belongs to SB-1.
Records where SB-2 stands, such as its next action, so the work can resume once SB-1 ships.
Any code written for SB-2 is covered by tests of its acceptance criteria, and the existing tests are unchanged. A run that wrote no code for SB-2 makes this point.
